blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: FY2024 was a year of heavy refinancing, debt-funded acquisitions and a debt-funded special dividend. The 10-K states that "During fiscal 2024, the Company completed approximately $21,000 million in debt financing transactions, inclusive of new issuances and refinancing of existing debt" (10-K page 53). These are Documentary Facts unless the sentence says otherwise.

New debt and refinancing. On November 28, 2023 the company issued "$2,000 million in new senior debt ($1,000 million in 7.125% senior secured notes due 2031 and $1,000 million in Tranche J term loans)", used to fund the acquisition of CPI's Electron Device Business and for general corporate purposes (10-K page 53). On February 27, 2024 it extended the revolving credit facility from May 2026 to February 2029, increased commitments "from $810 million to $910 million", and issued "$4,400 million in new secured debt ($2,200 million in 6.375% senior secured notes due 2029 and $2,200 million in 6.625% senior secured notes due 2032)" to redeem the 6.25% senior secured notes due 2026 (10-K page 53). On March 22, 2024 it repriced the Tranche I term loans, replaced Tranche H with Tranche K maturing March 2030, and issued "an additional $550 million in 6.375% senior secured notes due 2029" to redeem the 7.50% senior subordinated notes due 2027 (10-K page 53). On June 4, 2024 it repriced Tranche J and extended part of Tranche I into Tranche J maturing February 28, 2031 (10-K page 53). On July 12, 2024 it increased the securitization facility capacity "from $450 million to $650 million" (10-K page 53). On September 19, 2024 it issued "$3,000 million in new senior secured debt ($1,500 million in 6.00% senior secured notes due January 15, 2033 and $1,500 million in Tranche L term loans" (10-K page 54).

Acquisitions. The company completed SEI on May 21, 2024 "for approximately $171 million in cash", CPI's Electron Device Business on June 6, 2024 "for approximately $1,385 million in cash", and Raptor Scientific on July 31, 2024 "for approximately $647 million in cash" (10-K page 54). Total FY2024 acquisition spending appears in the CP-1 cash-flow table.

Special dividends. A special dividend of 35 US dollars per share was paid on November 27, 2023, "funded by existing cash on hand" (10-K page 54). On September 19, 2024, "concurrently with the $3,000 million issuance of new senior secured debt", the board declared a special dividend of 75 US dollars per share. The 10-K says total payments of "approximately $4,348 million" were "funded by a combination of $3,000 million in new senior secured debt (as previously noted) and existing cash on hand" and "were made in October 2024" (10-K page 54).

Subsequent events, after the as-of date and not part of FY2024 facts. The dividend was paid on October 18, 2024 (FY2025 Q1 10-Q page 44). The remaining securitization capacity was drawn in October 2024 (10-K page 152). During the first quarter of fiscal 2025 the company "repurchased 252,800 shares of common stock ... for a total amount of $316 million" (FY2025 Q1 10-Q page 44). At December 28, 2024 the issuer reported cash liquidity of "$ 3,308" in millions, made up of cash and revolver availability (FY2025 Q1 10-Q page 44). The 10-Q states again that "There is no maturity on any tranche of term loans or notes until November 2027" (FY2025 Q1 10-Q page 45).

Liquidity effect, as Analyst Interpretation: the September 2024 notes and term loans raised cash that left the company within a month as a shareholder distribution. The year-end cash balance in CP-1 therefore overstates the cash available to creditors, which is why CP-1 shows the issuer's pro forma cash liquidity and a labelled pro forma leverage sensitivity.
Executed terms of these instruments are not in the source set (CP-0). The descriptions above come from the 10-K narrative, not from indentures or credit agreement amendments.

fields.value: The expense block between gross profit and income from operations is selling and administrative expenses plus amortization of intangible assets, and it reconciles exactly in each year (C7). Total depreciation and amortization of 312 (10-K page 71) is a different, wider measure and is not the income-statement amortization line.

fields.value: Source: 10-K pages 144 to 145. The printed subtotal of 24,581 excludes the securitization row; the printed components add to it exactly (C10). Gross principal including securitization is 25,068 (C10, calculated). The MD&A "Total debt" of 24,880 is the net carrying amount including securitization (C11). The term loans are described as "$8,702 million in fully drawn term loans" with "an $910 million revolving credit facility" (10-K page 59). The 10-K states: "There is no maturity on any tranche of term loans or notes until November 2027 (fiscal 2028)" (10-K page 56).

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 10-K footnote states: "When considering the impact of the $4,348 million payment in special dividends and dividend equivalents in October 2024, the pro forma cash liquidity as of September 30, 2024 is $2,919 million." Revolver availability is after "$67 million in letters of credit outstanding" (10-K page 59). The securitization availability was drawn after the year end: "The Company drew the remaining $162.5 million available under the Securitization Facility in October 2024" (10-K page 152).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Source: 10-K page 71. Both reconciliations (from net income and from operating cash flow) reach the same EBITDA and EBITDA As Defined, and the net-income bridge adds exactly (C12).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Definition: EBITDA As Defined is issuer-defined. The 10-K says neither measure "is a measurement of financial performance under U.S. GAAP" (10-K page 71). Its add-backs include non-cash stock compensation and integration costs. The issuer itself notes that EBITDA As Defined "excludes the cash expense we have incurred to integrate acquired businesses" (10-K page 70).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant alignment: the issuer uses the name "As Defined", but the executed Credit Agreement is not supplied (CP-0). This handoff does not claim that EBITDA As Defined equals any covenant EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Depreciation and amortization of 312 equals depreciation of 149 plus "Amortization of intangible assets and product certification costs" of 163 from the cash-flow statement (10-K page 122). It is wider than the income-statement amortization line of 161.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The two reported quarters and the comparative first quarter add exactly to the printed year-to-date figures (C13). The fourth-quarter figure is derived and must stay labelled as calculated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage: total debt on a carrying basis rose from 19,750 to 24,880 while EBITDA As Defined rose from 3,395 to 4,173. Gross leverage on EBITDA As Defined moved from 5.82x to 5.96x; on reported EBITDA it is 6.53x. Mechanism: new term loans and secured notes funded acquisitions and special dividends (cash-flow lines above). Credit implication: leverage is high and rose slightly despite strong earnings growth. Net leverage at the year end is flattered by cash that was paid out as a dividend in October 2024; the labelled pro forma figure is 5.50x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Coverage: EBITDA As Defined covers net interest expense 3.24x in FY2024, up from 2.92x. Cash interest paid of 1,158 is lower than the expense of 1,286; the 10-K footnote shows interest in the operating-cash reconciliation excludes amortization of issuance costs and discount (10-K page 71). About 77% of gross debt was fixed rate (10-K page 55), so coverage is partly protected from rate moves; the hedge detail is not analysed here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash flow quality: operating cash flow rose from 1,375 to 2,045 and free cash flow (CFO less capex) from 1,236 to 1,880. Capex is small relative to sales. Working-capital lines absorbed cash in FY2024 (receivables and inventories printed as outflows, 10-K page 123). The gap between EBITDA As Defined and operating cash flow is mainly cash interest and cash taxes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity: reported cash liquidity of 7,267 at the year end falls to a pro forma 2,919 after the October 2024 dividend payment, as stated by the issuer. No debt matures until November 2027. The securitization facility was fully drawn in October 2024.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: FY2024 was a year of heavy refinancing, debt-funded acquisitions and a debt-funded special dividend. The 10-K states that "During fiscal 2024, the Company completed approximately $21,000 million in debt financing transactions, inclusive of new issuances and refinancing of existing debt" (10-K page 53). These are Documentary Facts unless the sentence says otherwise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt and refinancing. On November 28, 2023 the company issued "$2,000 million in new senior debt ($1,000 million in 7.125% senior secured notes due 2031 and $1,000 million in Tranche J term loans)", used to fund the acquisition of CPI's Electron Device Business and for general corporate purposes (10-K page 53). On February 27, 2024 it extended the revolving credit facility from May 2026 to February 2029, increased commitments "from $810 million to $910 million", and issued "$4,400 million in new secured debt ($2,200 million in 6.375% senior secured notes due 2029 and $2,200 million in 6.625% senior secured notes due 2032)" to redeem the 6.25% senior secured notes due 2026 (10-K page 53). On March 22, 2024 it repriced the Tranche I term loans, replaced Tranche H with Tranche K maturing March 2030, and issued "an additional $550 million in 6.375% senior secured notes due 2029" to redeem the 7.50% senior subordinated notes due 2027 (10-K page 53). On June 4, 2024 it repriced Tranche J and extended part of Tranche I into Tranche J maturing February 28, 2031 (10-K page 53). On July 12, 2024 it increased the securitization facility capacity "from $450 million to $650 million" (10-K page 53). On September 19, 2024 it issued "$3,000 million in new senior secured debt ($1,500 million in 6.00% senior secured notes due January 15, 2033 and $1,500 million in Tranche L term loans" (10-K page 54).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions. The company completed SEI on May 21, 2024 "for approximately $171 million in cash", CPI's Electron Device Business on June 6, 2024 "for approximately $1,385 million in cash", and Raptor Scientific on July 31, 2024 "for approximately $647 million in cash" (10-K page 54). Total FY2024 acquisition spending appears in the CP-1 cash-flow table.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Special dividends. A special dividend of 35 US dollars per share was paid on November 27, 2023, "funded by existing cash on hand" (10-K page 54). On September 19, 2024, "concurrently with the $3,000 million issuance of new senior secured debt", the board declared a special dividend of 75 US dollars per share. The 10-K says total payments of "approximately $4,348 million" were "funded by a combination of $3,000 million in new senior secured debt (as previously noted) and existing cash on hand" and "were made in October 2024" (10-K page 54).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Subsequent events, after the as-of date and not part of FY2024 facts. The dividend was paid on October 18, 2024 (FY2025 Q1 10-Q page 44). The remaining securitization capacity was drawn in October 2024 (10-K page 152). During the first quarter of fiscal 2025 the company "repurchased 252,800 shares of common stock ... for a total amount of $316 million" (FY2025 Q1 10-Q page 44). At December 28, 2024 the issuer reported cash liquidity of "$ 3,308" in millions, made up of cash and revolver availability (FY2025 Q1 10-Q page 44). The 10-Q states again that "There is no maturity on any tranche of term loans or notes until November 2027" (FY2025 Q1 10-Q page 45).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity effect, as Analyst Interpretation: the September 2024 notes and term loans raised cash that left the company within a month as a shareholder distribution. The year-end cash balance in CP-1 therefore overstates the cash available to creditors, which is why CP-1 shows the issuer's pro forma cash liquidity and a labelled pro forma leverage sensitivity.

fields.value: Evidence quality: High for the 10-K and 10-Q statements (primary, dated, issuer-specific). Management characterisations are quoted and not adopted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue durability. Evidence: high proprietary and aftermarket content and defense exposure (10-K pages 4 and 9). Mechanic: aftermarket and defense demand follow the installed fleet and government budgets more than new-aircraft deliveries, which supports revenue visibility. Implication: supports debt service at a high leverage level; the commercial OEM share remains exposed to Boeing and Airbus production rates (10-K page 11).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: CP-1 EBITDA As Defined margin and free cash flow; issuer pricing strategy (10-K page 5). Mechanic: margins depend on the ability to price proprietary parts; a pricing challenge from customers or governments would reduce cash available for interest. Implication: coverage per CP-1 C4 has room for some margin pressure; it is not tested against a scenario here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Concentration risk. Evidence: top ten customers at about 42% of net sales, none above 10% (10-K page 17). Mechanic: distributors and OEMs concentrate purchasing; loss of a large account would reduce volume. Implication: moderate concentration; monitor distributor relationships.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Shareholder alignment. Evidence: debt-funded special dividend in September 2024 and the stated priority order (10-K page 54). Mechanic: the issuer re-levers when earnings grow, so leverage stays high and the secured share of the capital structure grows. Implication: creditors should not expect deleveraging; leverage tolerance and refinancing depend on continued market access before the first maturity in November 2027. Counter-evidence: no maturity before November 2027 and large reported liquidity at the year end. The logged dividend-equivalent conflict does not change this view.
